fieldValues.title: WG Third-party ready: cycle close 2026-10-26
fieldValues.chose:
WG Third-party ready: cycle 2026-10-25 11:30 to 2026-10-26 11:30 UTC

1. Decisions for you: five open escalations, all proposed in the group log; one is new this run.
- NEW c16c70c1 (srs-rust#1481, release gate): may the release's conformance gate also run the RFC-043 arrangement fixture? Why it matters: a release is what every client pins, so this decides whether spec drift stops a release or only shows in CI. The tests themselves are within mandate; one workflow line is not, so the reviewer rejected and sent it to you. Options: (A) merge as is, drift holds a release at once; (B) land the tests now and ask for the gate line as its own PR; (C) tests only, the gate never changes. Recommendation: B. Action needed: decide. Urgency: low (owner-merge PR, nothing blocked).
- bf4a5af5 (srs-rust#1264, about 107h): how structured diagnostics reach the existing text lists. Why it matters: every reader of those lists breaks on the day the new build is pinned. Options: A replace everywhere; B structured list beside the text one; C code on validation results first; D nothing. Recommendation: C then B. Action needed: decide. Urgency: medium; srs-rust#1339 and #1342 wait behind it.
- 01cfb06e (srs-rust#1342, about 93h): type ErrorReport.details only for codes clients act on. Recommendation: the narrow mirror (option d). Action needed: decide. Urgency: low.
- 6b5e2810 (srs#931, about 40h): may an RFC reopen RFC-039's retired field-id bridge? Recommendation: authorise an RFC weighing "fieldId beside name" against "a separate resolution read". Action needed: decide. Urgency: low.
- 444121a6 (srs#911, about 28h): how a rendered document starts below its title (heading outline). Recommendation: open an RFC weighing a negative depthOffset against "first level follows the title". Action needed: decide. Urgency: low.
Also waiting on you: exercises dd1a47a7 (relation reads and createdBy, srs-rust#1411) and 2ac083c0 (one unknown key makes a repository unloadable). needs-input with no ruling: srs-rust#861, #683, #1198, #1132, #1380, srs#928.

2. Decided within mandate: nothing ratified by the group this cycle. No merged PR named a proposed decision as assent, so no group session was held. No owner ruling was made in either log this cycle.

3. Done: 3 PRs merged, all gate:auto-merge, builder agent:tpr-builder / reviewer agent:tpr-reviewer.
- srs-rust#1465 (refuse a type write that would orphan records, #1412): mandate RFC-039 [R19] / I-83; approve on green 4949034 after a re-review on the updated branch; 12:51.
- srs-rust#1480 (refuse retiring a relation type while Relations use the key): mandate RFC-006 V5 / remedy 89d74184; approve on green af160f2; 17:30.
- srs-rust#1482 (record fork carries the original's meta and tags): mandate rfc-decision-2e0cd70a; approve on green d707c15; 17:30.
Every merged PR has a quorum line with "findings: none".

4. Stuck or lost: four group PRs open.
- srs-rust#1481 (run the RFC-043 arrangement fixture): gates green, reviewer rejected as an escalation (see section 1), labelled owner-merge.
- srs-rust#1479 (refuse a relation-type key another definition holds): approved on green 99f1054, but the branch now conflicts with base; the Builder owns the merge.
- srs-rust#1469 (composition shown-in query): still behind base and red on the schema-mirror check since 10-24; nothing to merge until the builder syncs the mirror.
- srs#974 (conformance: [R11] json depth scenario): approved on green adc19ed but behind master; it needs a base update before it can merge.
No claims to release. srs-rust#1473 (new definition version beside the old, owner-approved, P1) has no PR yet.

5. Budget: 3 of 10 delegated merges this cycle; 4 open. Pause state: running (the 10-25 report is not yet acknowledged; one unacknowledged report does not pause). clerk group-state reads 0 merged because this run started after the 11:30 roll-over; the figure is counted from the PRs.
5b. Awaiting ratification: bf4a5af5 (about 107h), 01cfb06e (about 93h), 6b5e2810 (about 40h), 444121a6 (about 28h), c16c70c1 (new). Session to ratify: `clerk session --as owner --repo <srs-programme> --ratify all` (the-greenman/clerk; the TUI is `clerk --as owner`).

6. Next: ready and workable: 1 (srs-rust#1476, the retired relation type still holds its key; it was blocked by #1475, which #1480 now resolves). Every other `ready` issue is needs-input or parked. Top 3 in the Builder's order, no local priorities set: srs-rust#1473 (P1, owner-approved), srs-rust#1476 (P2), srs-rust#1378 (P2, PR #1469). Open group PRs in flight: 4. Budget left: 7. **Queue running dry: 1 ready, budget 10. Needs feeding.** Your rulings on bf4a5af5 and 01cfb06e release srs-rust#1264, then #1339 and #1342; after that, the analyst's nominations and the drift list. Waits on you: section 1. Fed by the analyst: 2026-10-25 12:19 run: filed 6 (domain 2, rulings 2, conformance 2); the merged #1480 and #1482 came from it.
6b. Exercises: two open, both the group's own (not in the SemanticOps log): dd1a47a7 "Relation reads hide who asserted a link" (input asked for: should relation list and context reads carry createdBy, notes and meta, srs-rust#1411); 2ac083c0 "One unknown key makes a whole repository unloadable" (non-fatal diagnostic or fail-closed with the LOAD verb narrowed to meta).

7. What we learned: the analyst-to-builder-to-reviewer path worked end to end inside one day (srs-rust#1475 and #1478 filed, then built, reviewed and merged as #1480 and #1482), so a fed queue is the group's limit, not review. The gate boundary also held: the reviewer caught a one-line workflow change inside an otherwise in-mandate test PR. Build trigger: well over 10 ratified decisions are on record, so srs-web#560 (decision-log lens) is still ready to unpark; flagged again.
fieldValues.rationale: One new escalation was raised: srs-rust#1481 adds the RFC-043 arrangement fixture to the release corpus-conformance gate, a gate change outside the group boundary that no recorded ruling covers (c16c70c1). The four older escalations were already open as proposed decisions, so no second record was filed for them.
